content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent tests that match project risk and execution cost. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to choose test helpers, generate data, and structure assertions.
actual_capabilities: Selects between IntegrationTest, RdbTest, ControllerTest, RedisTest, MockingUnitTest, and PojoUnitTest.
Applies Given-When-Then structure to Java test cases.
Uses AssertJ patterns for values, collections, booleans, exceptions, and Optional results.
Provides Mockito setup and verification patterns for service unit tests.
Guides Fixture Monkey usage for test data creation.
Recommends when integration tests are justified for money, rollback, constraints, events, or workflows.
limitations: It assumes Java 17, Spring Boot 3.2 or later, and JUnit 5 conventions.
It does not inspect a repository automatically unless the assistant is asked to read project files.
Project-specific helper classes must already exist or be replaced with standard Spring test annotations.
External service behavior is expected to be mocked during integration tests.

use_cases.title: Service Test Selection
use_cases.description: Choose MockingUnitTest or IntegrationTest before writing service tests for business logic.

use_cases.title: Repository and Query Testing
use_cases.description: Write focused RdbTest cases for repository behavior, QueryDSL queries, and database constraints.

use_cases.title: Team Test Standardization
use_cases.description: Review test code for naming, display names, Given-When-Then structure, and AssertJ assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Test Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for selecting the right helper.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Allra test writing standard to choose the right test type for this Java Spring scenario: [describe scenario]. Explain the choice briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Service Unit Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for Mockito and AssertJ patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a MockingUnitTest for this service method using Given-When-Then, Mockito, AssertJ, and Allra naming rules: [paste method and dependencies].

prompt_templates.title: Build Repository Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create RdbTest cases for this repository or QueryDSL query. Cover success, empty result, and constraint behavior where relevant: [paste repository code].

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Test Suite
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for reviewing existing tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Java tests against the Allra test writing standard. Identify helper misuse, missing Given-When-Then structure, weak assertions, and unnecessary integration tests: [paste tests].

output_examples.input: A service method validates a user grade and calculates a discount.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends MockingUnitTest, lists repository mocks, names the test calculateDiscount_VipUser_10Percent, and uses AssertJ for the discount value.

output_examples.input: A workflow creates a contract, account, and funding record in one transaction.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends IntegrationTest because multiple tables and rollback behavior must be verified with real persistence.

output_examples.input: A controller endpoint returns a user response by ID.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends ControllerTest with a mocked service, HTTP status checks, and JSON response assertions.

best_practices: Start with MockingUnitTest unless the workflow needs real persistence, rollback, constraints, events, or multi-service coordination.
Keep every test readable with DisplayName, Given-When-Then sections, and specific AssertJ assertions.
Mock external payment, notification, and API systems even inside integration tests.
anti_patterns: Do not use IntegrationTest for simple validation, mapping, calculation, or single-entity service logic.
Do not omit verification for important mocked collaborator calls.
Do not write tests whose names hide the method, scenario, or expected result.

faq.question: When should I use IntegrationTest?
faq.answer: Use it for money flows, rollback behavior, multiple table consistency, database constraints, events, or workflows requiring several services.

faq.question: When is MockingUnitTest enough?
faq.answer: Use it for most service business logic, validation, calculations, data conversion, and simple CRUD behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill require Fixture Monkey?
faq.answer: No. Fixture Monkey is recommended for test data generation, but project-specific factories can also be used.

faq.question: Can external APIs be called in integration tests?
faq.answer: No. The standard expects external payment, notification, and API clients to be mocked.

faq.question: What naming style does the skill use?
faq.answer: It recommends method_scenario_result test method names and clear DisplayName text for intent.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex apply this to existing tests?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask the assistant to read the tests, compare them with the standard, and propose focused changes.
